frequency_question: What proportion of major federal bills complete the required legislative steps and pass the Senate within a 314-day window?
membership_rule: Includes bills introduced in the U.S. Senate that reach committee and floor debate stages; excludes simple resolutions, joint resolutions on narrow administrative matters, and emergency measures expedited by unanimous consent.

cases.name: Tax Relief for American Families and Workers Act

coverage_note: 8 named; believed roughly 20 comparable major standalone bills in total during the window.
known_gaps: Excludes minor naming bills and unanimous consent items which bypass standard scheduling friction.
skeleton: Legislative cycles across two Congresses (117th and 118th), sampling major standalone statutory bills tracked from introduction to final Senate passage within a sub-year timeframe.
multiplier: 8 cases sampled; 5 hits within 314 days, 3 misses due to time expiration.
validity_reason: Remains stable through the duration of current Senate standing rules and typical procedural pacing.
